say.en: A survey company must reach 10,000 farmers across Karnataka in two weeks. Should it send people, letters or make phone calls? In this lesson: Compare personal interview, mail and telephone methods.
Explain the purpose of a pilot survey.

body.en: Personal interview: the investigator meets respondents face to face; high response and clarity, but costly and the interviewer may influence answers. Mailing questionnaire: cheap and wide-reaching, but low response and only for literate people. Telephone interview: quick and cheaper than visits, but only for people with phones and easy to refuse.
body.kn: ವೈಯಕ್ತಿಕ ಸಂದರ್ಶನ: ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯೆ, ಆದರೆ ದುಬಾರಿ. ಅಂಚೆ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾವಳಿ: ಅಗ್ಗ, ಆದರೆ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯೆ. ದೂರವಾಣಿ ಸಂದರ್ಶನ: ವೇಗ, ಆದರೆ ಫೋನ್ ಇರುವವರಿಗೆ ಮಾತ್ರ.

title.en: On the board: Three ways to reach people

say.en: There are three modes of collecting primary data.
Personal interview: face to face, highest response, but costly.
Mailing: cheap and wide, but few reply and only literate people can answer.
Telephone: quick and cheaper than visits, but only for people with phones.
Before the main survey we try the questionnaire on a small group: the pilot survey.
On the board: Three ways to reach people.

prompt.en: Match each mode of survey with its main feature.
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಸಮೀಕ್ಷಾ ವಿಧಾನವನ್ನು ಅದರ ಮುಖ್ಯ ಲಕ್ಷಣದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಸಿ.

right.en: Face to face: high response and doubts cleared, but costly, and the interviewer may influence answers
Cheap and reaches a wide area, but the response is low and no one is there to explain a question
Quick and cheaper than visits, but reaches only people with phones and cannot watch reactions
A trial run on a small group to find unclear questions, the time and the cost
A trained person who asks the questions and fills in the schedule

explanation.en: Each mode trades cost against accuracy and response. A pilot survey is done before the main survey to improve the questionnaire.

problem.en: Suggest the best mode for each: (a) a study of literacy among elderly villagers, (b) a quick opinion poll of city mobile users, (c) a survey of college principals across India.

steps.en: (a) Many may not read: personal interview.
(b) Speed matters and all have phones: telephone interview.
(c) Literate, widely scattered: mailing (or e-mail) questionnaire.
